title: scene-loop-copies-param-inert
description: Scene Loop modifier: the Copies row (scene_array.count, whitelisted in scene_modifier.rs LOOP_ROW_WHITELIST) does nothing — dragging it produces no visible change. Evidence from Peter screenshot 2026-09-05: Stride=3 but Copies=8 (coupled write stride_to_count says count=stride+2 capped at 8 — a live coupling would read 5), so count is stale OR the write never reaches the renderer OR the instance array is built once and never re-derived. Questions: does scene_array consume count live at VM eval or build-time? Is count re-derived from stride anywhere per-eval, stomping user writes? Does the Copies row id join to the stamped param (sync shows 8, so the read path works)? Fix must keep INV-4 (camera travel == instance spacing) truthful — if count is derived, either the coupling runs both directions (Copies drag sets stride=count-2) or the row goes. Root cause unknown — verify against code.
close_reason: Landed on main in merge of lane/scene-modifier-copies (6699d672a lane work). Root cause: scene_array buffer capacity sized from count VALUE at plan pre-allocation; every live count write clamped invisible. Fix: capacity = count range max, WGSL masks surplus slots to zero-scale (main+shadow, standalone+fused). Gates: renderer 1754 passed, clippy clean, gpu_proofs PASS, landing gate green.

title: scene-modifier-card-drag-clunky
description: Click and drag on inspector scene modifier cards (SCENE_MODIFIER_FRAMEWORK) feels clunky/dead — drags appear to snap back or not engage. Suspects from lead review: (1) param_card/routing.rs drag emission sites hard-code GraphParamTarget::Generator for Generator-kind cards instead of the modifier-aware self.param_target() (mod.rs ~590 returns GeneratorOf(layer_id)); relight path already uses param_target(); (2) scrub begin gate in ui_bridge/scrub.rs requires inst.params.contains(param_id) — a modifier row id that misses the stamped params map opens no scrub session and the value snaps back on next sync; (3) mid-drag structural sync rebuilding modifier cards, killing node ids mid-gesture. Root cause unknown — verify against code. Fix shape: route modifier rows through the same live-scrub path effect card rows use, with a regression test that a drag Move writes the value and the value survives the next sync_card_values pass.
close_reason: Landed on main in merge of lane/scene-modifier-drag (commit 80b657bb3 lane work, merge 6daacfbad). Root cause: modifier card drags re-derived GraphParamTarget::Effect(0) from self.kind for mid-gesture moves + commit; all drag emissions now ride param_target() = GeneratorOf(owning layer). Gates: nextest 1243 passed, clippy clean, 15/15 required ui-flows, landing gate 6/0.

title: audition-grid page fault: pool recycling races in-flight command buffers (ParticleText)
description: Audition grid page-fault → queue blacklist → exit(70). Symptom: open generators browser with a generator layer playing; first GPU error is a page fault (code=3) in a compositor-path buffer, then every buffer is Ignored and ContentPipeline exits (content_pipeline.rs:1634). Reproduced headlessly: lane/audition-fault-repro, solo sweep of ParticleText (2M active particles) faults 4/4 when prior ContentThread create/drop churn precedes it; full 27-cell grid at 300 frames, master tap, layer tap, reopen-realloc all clean (fault needs short lists so the heavy cell renders every frame). Mechanism (attributed, one step unproven): TexturePool recycling is frame-counter-paced, safe only when encode stays ≤3 frames ahead of GPU completion; ParticleText sustained load opens the reuse-while-in-flight window across concurrently in-flight command buffers. Same class as BUG-rnnr (RT denoiser mode-switch realloc, open P1 — identical signature). Class fix: fence-aware pool retirement (texture_pool.rs doc names this as the stated escape hatch) — removes the pacing assumption rather than tightening it. Evidence: /tmp/audition_repro_*.log in the lane worktree; repro module crates/manifold-app/src/audition_fault_repro.rs (unlanded).
notes:
LEAD ANALYSIS 2026-09-05: the pacing wait IS GPU-completion-based (native_event is signaled on the content command buffer, content_pipeline.rs:3357), so the live frame loop honors the pool contract — live attribution of the crash to the pool is still UNPROVEN; the harness reproduced only the unpaced condition. Export mode encodes with no presentation wait — an unpaced live path that shares the pool. BUG-rnnr (RT denoiser realloc) remains a live-attribution candidate; Peter first-error log line discriminates. Class fix stands regardless: fence-aware retirement removes the assumption (texture_pool.rs doc names it as the escape hatch).
DISPROOF (pool-fence-fix lane, commit ed287e617 on lane/pool-fence-fix): fence-aware recycling implemented and confirmed attached — repro still faults (frame moved, different preset on rerun); recycling disabled ENTIRELY — fault still reproduces (ParticleText@28). Conclusion: the faulting texture is NOT pool-recycled; the BUG-l7t4 mechanism is elsewhere. Live suspects: chain-runtime internal caches (StateStore/memo direct textures), audition surface IOSurface import, cross-encoder hazard (first fault is always a page fault on the Compositor command buffer; Generators CB runs as a separate in-flight buffer). The fence-aware pool fix landed anyway (frame-counter recycling was documented-unsound on unpaced paths — export, headless — with the named escape hatch); BUG-rnnr confirmed NOT pool-backed (denoise/RT targets are direct create_texture fields reallocated instantly on switch) — needs its own retire-before-reuse fix.
MECHANISM CONFIRMED (fault-mechanism lane, commit 5b3b09f75 on lane/fault-mechanism): heap-pool texture UAF across in-flight command buffers. TexturePool is MTLHeap-backed (device.rs:1676); heap sub-allocation memory is reusable while an in-flight CB still references the old sub-allocation. Teardown/drop paths release heap textures BARE — drop-site backtraces: MetalBackend::replace_texture_2d (metal_backend.rs:301) via PresetRuntime::install_target (preset_runtime/core.rs:2026), GeneratorRenderer per-layer (LayerId, GpuTexture) map teardown. Discriminators: per-frame queue drain → fault gone; HOLD_CHURN (no prior ContentThread drop) → no fault; defer BOTH textures+buffers 8 frames → gone; textures-only deferral → gone. The churn ContentThread teardown drops pooled heap textures; the new run reallocates the same heap memory while the churn CBs still execute → GPU Address Fault attributed to the heavy Compositor CB. The landed fence-aware pool fix covers the RECYCLE path only, not bare drops. Open sub-question: whether missing useResource on the RENDER-pass binding path (encoder.rs — dispatch path has it at 494/499, render pass does not) is also load-bearing. Probe oracle: control faults 4/4 at frame 15 (solo ParticleText, layer tap); drain/defer both clean.
Probes re-verified on main tip 2c0428e11 (lane/fault-mechanism = main + probe commit 5b3b09f75, landing-ready): control faults frame 15 exact signature; deferral clean 40 frames. New scope data: the faulting Compositor/Generators CB scopes name the StarField clip chain (gen L0 StarField) as a sampler of the racing heap-pool transient — corroborates heap-UAF attribution (fault lands on whichever CB executes at detection). Probe branch: lane/fault-mechanism, sole holder.
FINAL (heap-retire-fix lane, e84860a9d on lane/heap-retire-fix): fence-stamped drop retirement implemented and verified (manifold-gpu retire.rs; marks on every texture class + buffers; mpsc, any-thread drops; per-frame drain + teardown flush; 6 new unit tests, nextest 2133, clippy clean) — but the NO-OP discriminator (zero hold, full probe path) is CLEAN, exonerating resource drops entirely. The fault is a sub-frame-tight timing race cured only by per-frame quiescence (DRAIN) or any per-frame CPU perturbation. Refine next probe toward: encode-ahead overlap hazards NOT involving drop lifetime (e.g. shared-mode resources read by an in-flight earlier frame while a later frame rewrites/retargets them; cross-frame aliasing of transient bindings). NOTE: machine GPU driver is sticky-degraded from this session repros (BUG-gtrs reproduced on base uncontended) — any further GPU probing requires a reboot first. The retirement hardening lands post-reboot alongside BUG-rnnr; both gated on clean gpu_proofs.

title: Scene Loop black on imported scene - camera flies through solid mesh
description: BUG-aahp (Scene Loop renders black on imported scene): probe lane result. In-process real-path delivery (GeneratorRegistry::create_with_override + runtime.render on the applied apricot import) resolves loop-node RUNTIME params to the PLAN values (loop_camera home=-5.19, cell_size=10.39, beat_ramp rate=0.125) — manifest/exposure drops do NOT clobber them (theories 1+2 refuted on the delivery path). The black is a GEOMETRY result: loop_camera flies through the SOLID mesh interior for most of the loop. Recentered import z-span = symmetric +-cell/2 = -5.19..+5.19. Camera at home=-cell/2 (beat 0) is at the near face — renders a few lit pixels (18/16384 px, max 234). At beats 1/3/7 (phase 0.125/0.375/0.875) the camera is INSIDE the solid tree (z=-3.89/-1.30/+3.90) — pure black. The D10 "corridor" framing assumes a hollow scenic volume; a solid tree occludes the camera for the whole middle+end of the loop. The throwaway headless harness renders the real import near-black even UNAPPLIED (0 px lit), so harness cannot show the app baseline; but the applied beat-0 corridor view (18 px) being nonzero PROVES the splice delivers pixels and the black at beats 1-7 is the camera-in-mesh, not a dropped wire/param. Also: ignored gate scene_loop_import_wrap_parity_phases_match FAILS diff=87 (lead cited 149) on the shared device (comment claims 0) — beats 0/8 phase wrap mismatches on the real import. Suspect shape for the fix: home should be placed at the near face of the SOLID volume with the camera looking AWAY from occlusion, or keep the camera OUTSIDE the mesh (farther home + look-in). Probe scratch test untracked in worktree slot-1, not committed.

title: BUG-upfq follow-up: embedded-scene presets keep generic bands
description: Symptom: pre-2026-08-15 projects (Right Where I Need You v5 ALT, sakura/apricot photoscans) keep generic slider bands (distance 0.01-100, far 1-10000) despite the scene-scale repair passes. Root cause, two stacked holes: (A) scene_bounds is stamped only at GLB import (gltf_import/scene.rs:884) and was introduced 2026-08-15 — older projects have it None everywhere, so scene_exposure pass 4 falls back to generic metadata bands; (B) the load-time exposure migration never runs on embedded preset defs at all — install_embedded_presets -> preset_loader::set_project_presets has no migrate_scene_exposures call, and the project_io.rs load loop only touches layer-inline graphs (these layers carry graph: None; the def lives in embeddedPresets). Verified against the actual file: 27 embedded presets, zero scene_bounds, generic stamped ranges. Fix shape: app-seam load backfill — for each embedded scene def lacking scene_bounds, read the GLB JSON chunk only (accessor POSITION min/max x node transforms, no buffer decode), stamp scene_bounds, run migrate_scene_exposures on the project.embedded_presets defs BEFORE install/reconcile, so bands repair and persist on next save. Missing coverage that let this slip twice: no load-time test with a pre-scene_bounds embedded scene preset.
close_reason: Fixed by lane/scene-embedded-bounds-backfill (main 5067e9d5d). Load-time backfill reads the GLB JSON chunk, stamps scene_bounds on embedded scene presets, re-runs the scene-exposure migration, refreshes the overlay + reconciles manifests. Landing gate green: clippy, tests, GPU proofs.

title: collect-all-skips-glb-in-embedded-presets-without-file_path-flag
description: Collect All and Save silently skips GLB/HDRI paths in projects with embedded presets authored before the file_path flag existed (2026-09-02). Symptom: V5 of "Right Where I Need You" collected audio only; 10 generator layers still load GLBs from /Users/peterkiemann/MANIFOLD - Rust/tests/fixtures/gltf/ — breaks off-machine. Root cause: inventory (manifold-io collect.rs resolve_string_defs) is flag-driven and embedded preset metadata shadows the registry def; embedded presets carry isFilePicker: true but no file_path flag (serde default false). Any pre-flag project with embedded presets is affected. Fix shape: inventory treats a string param as a file path when the embedded def has is_file_picker plus an extension-classifiable value, or unions the flag from the registry def for the same param id; alternatively a load-time migration backfills the flag into embedded presets.
close_reason: Fixed in P5 (42fe6c300): collection follows the stringBinding to the file_loader_kind table; flags no longer consulted. Embedded presets collect their GLBs.

title: Temporal-upscale conditioning: fix blur/detail loss, add global + export columns
description: Peter tried scene temporal_upscale (renders 2/3 linear = DLSS-Quality ratio, render_scene.rs:285): works but blurs and loses fine detail. The MTL4 scaler model is current (metalfx_temporal_upscaler.rs prefers Metal4FxTemporalScaler) so the model is not the problem — the feed is. Suspects in order: (1) double temporal filtering — ~40-frame irradiance accumulator under the scalers own temporal pass softens detail; (2) reactive mask unwired — movers/emissives smear into history (August notes flagged both as confounds in the rejected denoised-scaler look); (3) jitter/velocity validation — misaligned frame averaging reads exactly as fine-detail blur. Target: DLSS-Quality-like, near-native. If still soft after conditioning, bump RT_TEMPORAL_RENDER_SCALE to 3/4 (one-line constant). Also in scope: temporal upscale joins the RT_QUALITY_SETTINGS quality columns — global project toggle with per-scene override; export column defaults to native full-res (exports never need the upscaler). Pairs with BUG-eytk (spatial a-trous denoiser): a denoised correctly-masked input is what lets the temporal scaler look like DLSS.

title: Spatial a-trous denoiser between RT accumulation and post effects (stage 3)
description: The missing third denoising stage: variance-guided a-trous wavelet filter using existing G-buffers (depth/normal/roughness already emitted as MetalFX feeds). Irradiance already demodulated so filtering is safe. Kills boiling where accumulation is weak (motion, disocclusion, post-light-gesture frames) and is the export-time lever: filtering is ~1-2ms, rays are the expensive input, so same quality at a fraction of the trace cost. Supersedes the BUG-312 depth-only-bilateral upgrade note in RAYTRACING_DESIGN.md section 17. Design before code.

title: Export dies on AVAssetWriter WriterNotReady mid-encode (no backpressure wait)
description: Symptom: 2026-08-26 real section export (Right Where I Need You, 720x1280@24) died in section 5 at frame 318: encode_frame failed WriterNotReady → export aborted. Four prior sections fine. Root cause: MetalEncoderPlugin append path never waits on AVAssetWriterInput.readyForMoreMediaData — appendPixelBuffer failure is treated as fatal instead of backpressure. Latent in single-export too; long section runs + machine load (RT rebuilds, freeze compiles, concurrent cargo builds) make the writer fall behind. Fix shape: bounded wait/retry on readyForMoreMediaData (KVO or polling with timeout) in the append path of MetalEncoderPlugin.m before appendPixelBuffer; error only on genuine timeout. Repro: export a multi-section range on a busy machine.
close_reason: Fixed on main: append path waits on readyForMoreMediaData (10s bound, logged) instead of failing. Verification: Peter re-runs the Right Where I Need You section export.

Root cause: block_displace_field / scanline_jitter_field / flow_field_noise resolve an unwired time port from ctx.time.seconds in run(), but the freeze-fused kernel has no per-frame clock feed — time stays param-default 0.0, so floor(time*speed*12)=0 forever. Graph editor preview (unfused) is correct. Shipped since 36908fd43 (atoms made fusable) + 5ac56228e (per-card fusion in chain); standalone parity tests pack time explicitly so nothing caught it — no fused-animation proof exists. Fix shape: frame_time_inputs declaration in primitive! -> unwired declared ports route through the derived-uniform recompute path (frame seconds); wired keeps todays uniform path; source-scan scope test + fused-animation proofs.
close_reason: Closed

title: RT quality settings have no effect in the live app — missing ProjectAction::ChangeRtQuality handler in app_render.rs
description: Symptom: changing RT quality tiers or ray resolution in the RT Quality panel produces no visual or performance change in the live app. The panel dispatches ProjectAction::ChangeRtQuality, which is handled in ui_bridge/project.rs (headless/flows) but has NO handler in the live app_dispatch (crates/manifold-app/src/app_render.rs). The content thread resolves project.settings.rt_quality every frame and pushes to the compositor (proven plumbing), but the mutation never reaches the content thread_s project because the live app dispatcher drops the action. Fix: add a handler in app_render.rs around line 900 (near other PanelAction::Project handlers) following the SetAudioInputDevice pattern: read current settings from self.content_state.project.settings.rt_quality, construct ChangeRtQualityCommand::new(old, new), send via self.send_content_cmd(ContentCommand::Execute(Box::new(cmd))). 5 lines. Root cause: the P3 closeout commit added the UI bridge handler but forgot the live app dispatch. k3 (lead)
close_reason: Fixed two halves: app_render dispatch handler (b601ed45, main) + the deeper generator-renderer split-brain (wave/rt-quality-fix): content_pipeline now fans the per-frame column out to every ClipRenderer, GeneratorRenderer applies it to each PresetRuntime at render time. Verified via rt-capture A/B: quarter-res fixture traces at 864x558 vs 1728x1117 default. Panel reworked to real dropdowns in the same branch.

Committed version of the same fixture renders all channels fine. Structural diff of the two versions shows embeddedPresets (1 -> 3) is the ONLY change, so the load path turns two extra project-local khronos glTF presets into a dead RT scene. If this hits a real show project it reads as RT silently off. Fix shape: reproduce by embedding the two presets into any RT fixture, find where the scene/RT setup diverges on load. Evidence: /tmp/rte_disk.json + /tmp/rte_head.json (structural diff), /tmp/rte_committed.manifold (committed binary). k3 (lead)

title: RT denoiser mode-switch reallocates textures under in-flight frames — GPU page fault, queue blacklist, forced exit
description: Repro fingerprint: RT scene (surveillance_cam) with rt_denoise_feed on + temporal upscale, then a window resize while forced-outputs host rebuilds (BUG-18l) are churning. MetalFX classic denoiser created twice in consecutive frames (2304x1489->3456x2234 upscale mode, then 3456x2234->3456x2234 1:1 mode) while GPU was 4 frames behind; in-flight frames read aux/scratch textures reallocated to new dims by the mode switch -> MPS page fault (no bounds checks) in Generators command buffer, then SubmissionsIgnored blacklist and BUG-665r exit. Root cause: denoise-path mode/size switches reallocate targets instantly with no regard for in-flight frames. Fix shape: on denoise-path dim/mode change, keep retired targets alive and hold denoise_active off until the GPU drains past the last frame referencing them (frame-fence machinery already knows when). Removes the whole class (resize churn, rt_ready churn, upscale<->1:1 switch), not just this ordering. See render_scene.rs:4827-4856 (denoise_wanted gate + ensure_denoiser). Observed 2026-08-15 on main, M4 Max.

title: rt-kernel-toggle-sequence-breaks-raster-base-state
description: Peter repro in-app: RT off -> on with default kernels -> disable all kernels -> RT off -> RT on leaves the preview broken: raster base gone (only sparse dotted outline of the apricot visible) plus halo-like artifacts. RT Enabled ON + all kernels OFF should equal raster-only, so the RT master/kernel state machine is dropping the raster contribution or leaving a stale channel bound. Root cause unknown; suspects: render_scene RT state not rebuilt on kernel-mask change, stale temporal/accumulator buffer surviving the off->on cycle, or the all-kernels-off config taking a partial-RT composite path instead of pure raster. Sequence-dependent, so state, not shading.

title: manifold processes leak to ~30GB each; watchdog kernel panic from compressor exhaustion
description: Symptom: 2026-08-14 12:24 kernel panic (watchdog timeout, bug_type 210) — VM compressor exhausted (~18GB compressed, ratio 5, ~90GB anon) on 36GB M4 Max after 4.5d uptime. Panic process table: four manifold processes resident 29.9/28.6/26.5/15.1 GB (~100GB combined). Low pid 6933 (15.1GB) likely long-lived GUI app; high pids were lane-spawned headless RT renders (rt_toggle_matrix, rt_floor capture, release build mid-flight). Root cause: unknown — suspects: RT render path accumulation/capture buffers never freed, texture leak across graph rebuilds, per-render working set never released in headless mode. Fix shape: footprint profile of headless RT render over hundreds of frames (memory graph / leaks / vmmap), check capture-dir path frees frame buffers, audit texture cache eviction in graph runtime. Evidence: /Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/panic-full-2026-08-14-150927.0002.panic
notes:
2026-08-14 k3 (lead): panic thread tables identify all four processes. pid 6933 = long-lived GUI app (132 threads vs 12-14 in the renders) — slow leak ~15GB over 4.5d uptime. All four share an rt-capture-drain thread; the three young headless renders hit 26-30GB in <1h. Prime suspect: rt capture path queues frames for the drain thread without a bound — 4K RGBA16F ≈ 66MB/frame, 30GB ≈ 450 frames of un-drained queue. Check capture queue backpressure first.
2026-08-14 k3 (lead): reproduced locally. NOT a monotonic leak in the render processes: a single 4K rt-capture run spikes to 21-25GB phys_footprint within the first ~5s of rendering, then settles ~7.2GB for the rest of a 600-frame run. vmmap at spike: IOAccelerator 21.0G virt / 12.6G resident across ~220 regions of the 128MB class (= 4K Rgba32Float texture size) + 5.4G owned-unmapped graphics. So each 4K RT render carries a ~25GB startup transient; three lane runs overlapping = ~75GB instantaneous demand + 15GB long-lived app = compressor exhaustion. Root of the transient still open: ~200 texture-sized Metal allocations at RT startup — needs an allocation inventory (texture-creation logging) in the RT path. Also found: capture path triple-decodes every channel (drain_captures -> compute_rt_channel_stats + process_capture, and process_capture re-runs both) — 3 full 4K texture readbacks + f32 vecs per channel per capture event. GUI app slow growth (15GB/4.5d) remains a separate open question.
2026-08-14 k3 (lead): alloc census (MANIFOLD_GPU_ALLOC_LOG instrumentation, landed on feat/rt-mem-inventory in slot-4): 769 events / 7.42GB cumulative through manifold-gpu create_texture/create_buffer — well short of the ~18GB GPU-side spike, so heaps (device.rs newHeapWithDescriptor) and RT accel structures (raytrace.rs newAccelerationStructureWithSize, x2) bypass the log and hold the rest. Signals inside the log: 6 x 512MB bufshared (3.07GB, identical size = same data 6x); 53 x identical 1024x1024 Rgba16Float mips=11 textures in one graph-load burst (591MB); a (99/114/61MB) bufshared trio repeated 6x in the first 22 events; 30 x 1x1 preset_runtime_target_owner recreations; 7 x 66MB frame-sized staging buffers during graph load. Caller backtrace pass (MANIFOLD_GPU_ALLOC_BT) running next to name the owners. Triple-decode capture fix committed same branch.
2026-08-14 k3 (lead): caller census verdict — NO recreate loops in the big groups. 6x512MB + 6x{99/114/61}MB = pre_allocate_array_buffers (graph_loader.rs:1592), once per prewarmed preset (~6GB held before first frame, dropped after prewarm). 53x1K-mipmapped = render-target pool cold fill on frame 1, reused after. KEY STAGE-RISK FINDING (lane): pre_allocate_array_buffers is also reachable from install_layer_generator (clip-start path) — if generator runtimes rebuild per clip start/retrigger, every clip start re-allocates the full Array buffer set (hundreds of MB churn per event). That is the leading suspect for the GUI app slow growth (15GB/4.5d): long session, many clip starts, allocator/compressor churn. Verify: does the runtime cache per clip instance, or rebuild on retrigger?
2026-08-14 k3 (lead): CURE TEST VERDICT — prewarm hypothesis half-wrong. Baseline vs MANIFOLD_SKIP_PRESET_PREWARM (720p 60f): bufshared churn 5.98GB -> 0.25GB (23.6x), but peak RSS only 16.89 -> 16.05GB (-0.84GB). Prewarm buffers are churn, NOT residency. Render output identical (hit delta <0.001). Shipped: loop now opt-in via MANIFOLD_PRESET_PREWARM=1 (commit 10577cea, feat/rt-mem-inventory). STILL UNEXPLAINED: ~16GB peak RSS at 720p with only 7.5GB logged through manifold-gpu — unlogged suspects: MetalFX temporal upscaler internals (RtNoiseTesting likely upscales; allocations bypass create_texture entirely), IOSurface, driver-internal, CPU-side asset decode (GLB/EXR). Also noted: 6 codegen prewarm failures pre-exist on main (blob_overlay, draw_connections, draw_dots, draw_gauge, draw_markers, draw_ticks) — present in both runs, not caused by this work; separate bead candidate.
2026-08-14 k3 (lead): vmmap at peak (720p, 16.7GB RSS): IOAccelerator dominates — 224-243 regions, ~200 of them 128MB slabs, 13-15.6GB resident, empty region detail, resolution-INDEPENDENT. Not MALLOC, not IOSurface, not mapped files. MetalFX exonerated (1.05GB), prewarm exonerated for residency (0.84GB). THEORY: slabs are per-compile driver allocations from cold-compiling ~150+ pipelines — headless harness never loaded pipeline_cache.metallib/msl_cache (only app.rs GUI path did). Explains: resolution independence, logging invisibility, why freshly-built lane binaries were the worst case. FIX SHIPPED (d14faff5, feat/rt-mem-inventory): headless harness loads both caches, load-only (GUI owns the file; no headless save = no concurrent-write race). Verification run E pending — if peak drops multiple GB below the 16.05-16.89GB band, theory confirmed.
2026-08-14 k3 (lead): clip-start leak theory REFUTED by code read — install_layer_generator runs only on type swap / override-graph edit / watch toggle / relight change; param edits apply in place. Generator runtimes are cached per layer in layer_generators. Clip triggers reuse them. NEW SUSPECT for app creep: render_clip_thumbnail (generator_renderer.rs:1069) builds a SEPARATE generator instance per parked clip — if those are not cached, every thumbnail refresh allocates a full Array-buffer suite. Long UI session = slow churn. Check its caching first next session. LANDED: feat/rt-mem-inventory merged to main (04bde019) — decode-once, prewarm skip default, headless pipeline-cache load, alloc census instrumentation.
close_reason: Peter 2026-08-26: not a real leak — observed ~30GB/process was concurrent cargo builds during large parallel lane work, not steady-state app growth.

title: RT investigation: repeated toggle flips and combos leave stale state (user-observed)
description: Peter observes non-deterministic RT lighting in-app when flipping toggle combos on/off repeatedly and changing shadow type + lighting controls: scene goes "super dull" and stays. Proven instance: BUG-xyr0 (reflection history ~20% darker after rt_enabled off-on, never recovers). Next session: add matrix cells for (a) on-off-on identity — image must return to exact original, (b) combo sequences (shadows+AO+GI in different orders — order must not matter), (c) flip during live playback not just paused. Harness: scripts/rt_toggle_matrix.py. Suspects: accumulation/denoiser/irradiance history reset coverage (rt_denoise_feed and temporal_upscale are NOT in the toggle_flipped reset list, render_scene.rs ~4111), gate handoffs between RT and raster paths.
notes:
2026-08-14 k3 (lead): experiment design fix — all matrix flip cells and any new identity/combo cells MUST freeze the camera: non-paused rt-capture orbits the camera every frame, which view-confounds every cross-frame luma comparison (this invalidated the BUG-xyr0 numbers). Use --disable-driver-at 0 (freezes gen_param drivers from frame 0; verified: off-phase composite identical to 6 decimals across 80 frames). Identity cell shape: --disable-driver-at 0 --set-at 60 8_rt_enabled=0 --set-at 140 8_rt_enabled=1 --capture-every 20, then compare pre-off vs post-on composite at matched static view (holds on RtNoiseTesting as of d969071e). Combo cells: same shape with different --set-at orderings of rt_shadows/rt_ao/rt_gi/rt_reflections; final-state equivalence is the check, static camera makes it view-clean.
2026-08-14 k3 (lead): combo experiment battery on current main (d969071e), static camera, RtNoiseTesting: baseline vs combo-ao-gi vs combo-gi-ao vs combo-sh-refl vs combo-refl-sh vs all-terms-cycle vs rt-enabled-x2 (off-on-off-on) — final composite luma spread 0.08487..0.08503, max 1.6e-4 from baseline. Order-invariant, no stale state, repeated toggles clean. Headless MutateProject path is exonerated on THIS fixture. Remaining gaps to the in-app super-dull report: (1) fixture blindness — IBL-dominated floating car cannot show a stale sun/shadow term (BUG-gju4 floor fixture running in a lane); (2) app-side write path may differ from MutateProject (trace lane running); (3) shadow-TYPE changes and lighting scrubs mid-combo not yet covered; (4) denoise_feed/temporal_upscale interactions not in this battery. Logs: /tmp/rt_combo_*.log.

title: RT off-on cycle: 20% luma drop on re-enable
description: RT off-on cycle with terms off comes back ~20% darker (luma 0.082→0.066). NOT "nearly black" — scene stays lit but noticeably dimmer. Root cause: accumulated reflection history is ~25% darker after re-enable (refl_raw 0.246→0.196, refl_history 0.242→0.181). Moments count proves accumulation is warm (7.5→9.2), so not a reset issue. Sun term present (shadow maps render, shadow_factor falls through to raster). IBL term present (irradiance_map read, GI off in test). AO term present (irr.a≈1). Reflection term is the only difference: refl luma drops 20-25%, matching composite luma drop. Fix attempted: prevent TemporalResetDetector reset on rt_enabled 0→1 via rt_prev_rt_enabled/rt_prev_will_accumulate tracking. Result: moments count improved (now WARMER than baseline at 9.2), but reflection/composite still 20% darker. Reset not the root cause. Actual root cause: UNKNOWN. Reflection trace itself produces darker output despite warm accumulation and identical scene/params. Suspect: temporal reprojection fails across RT-off gap, or reflection history blends incorrectly. Fixture: RtNoiseTesting.manifold (envmap-lit car). Test: manifold rt-capture RtNoiseTesting.manifold --set-at 60 8_rt_enabled=0 --set-at 140 8_rt_enabled=1 --capture-every 20. Luma table: f40=0.082 (RT on), f100=0.089 (RT off), f160=0.066 (RT back on), f199=0.061 (stable darker).
notes: 2026-08-14 k3 (lead): NOT REPRODUCED on current main (d969071e) with a static camera. Original repro conflated viewpoint with state: non-paused rt-capture orbits the camera every frame, so f40 vs f160 compare different views of an envmap-lit car (refl luma swings ±20% by angle alone). Static rerun (--disable-driver-at 0, same set-at off/on): composite 0.085065 pre-off vs 0.085065 at f160 and 0.084980 at f199; refl_raw 0.2207 pre-off vs 0.2204 at f199. Identity holds. The "moments warm 9.2" reading was recovery-from-reset, not preserved warmth: the f143 capture shows a full reset (count 1) at re-enable — toggle_flipped fires because the rt_enabled-gated term values flip false→stored. Reset is benign for a static scene (signal re-converges to the same mean). Side observation: in the ORBITING run the composite sd exploded post-re-enable (0.35→19.7 by f199) while every captured RT channel stayed calm — unexplained, possibly view-dependent envmap glints; the zw2l static-camera combo cells will discriminate. Closing; the combo-flip hunt continues in BUG-zw2l.
close_reason: Closed

title: RT denoise flip: unify the engage decision — one gate, rebuild-on-flip (Peter directive)
description: Symptom: with rt_denoise_feed persisted on (value reaches the node at build), the frame where the denoiser first engages panics at render_scene.rs:6533 (specular_albedo_resolve_target.expect("denoise resolve texture allocated by plan")) — Peter live repro 2026-08-08, second panic after the BUG-7k1z session. Root cause (same class as the fixed hit-dist extract expect at 5703): the DN-E forward-pass aux-attachment builder (render_scene.rs ~6505-6535, four expects at 6512/6519/6526/6533 — normals/roughness/diffuse/specular albedo resolve targets) asserts plan allocation on the flip frame, which still runs the pre-flip plan. Fix shape: ONE gate — denoise_feed && all four resolve targets Some — else the forward pass runs without the aux MRT for exactly the flip frame (byte-identical to flag-off for that frame; the tail encode tuple guard already skips the denoise encode the same frame, so the whole denoise path idles one frame, D17 transition shape, pre-flip path presents). Do NOT fix expect-by-expect — audit every denoise_feed-gated plan-allocation read in evaluate and gate them together (5703 was fixed alone and 6533 fired immediately after; a third site would fire next). Evidence: crash-run log 08:59 — scaler created :51 then panic at 6533; BUG-7k1z (denoise toggle live flip inert) covers the card-row live-propagation half.
close_reason: Fixed on main e341370b: one denoise_aux_ready decision per evaluate drives pipeline variant, denoise_wanted, hit-dist extract, and all four aux-MRT attachments; flip frame idles byte-identical to flag-off, rebuilt plan engages next frame. Gate-block warn names aux_ready. Landing gate 6/6 incl gpu-proofs. Peter live-verify pending (flip RT Denoise Feed on brokenHelmetRotationsRT).

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text: Peter directive 2026-08-08: fix the CLASS, unified and safe — not expect-by-expect. Fix shape: compute ONE denoise_aux_ready = rt_denoise_feed && plan allocated the resolve targets, computed once per evaluate, and drive EVERY denoise production decision from it: the four aux-MRT attachment builders (~6512-6554), the forward-pass pipeline variant (emit_denoise_feed → aux_variant specialization + cache key, ~3089/3173/3183 and its call sites), the hit-dist extract (5703, already gated), and the tail encode (its tuple guard becomes this flag). denoise_active itself should require it. Byte-identical to flag-off for the flip frame; the rebuilt plan engages next frame. AND the bigger UX fix (with BUG-7k1z): the card toggle must trigger the host rebuild ON THE SPOT when flipped — Peter: "it should rebuild on the spot, loading the project again is the wrong design". rt_enabled flips already do this (forced-outputs epoch → host rebuild); give rt_denoise_feed the same live-rebuild path, then the degrade gate covers exactly the one transition frame.

comments.author: Peter Kiemann
comments.text:
CENSUS COMPLETE (4 lanes + lead spot-checks). Contract map:
1. RACE CONFIRMED: preview/node_preview/node_atlas bridges — content reuses an IOSurface slot gated only on its own write completion (is_surface_ready, content_pipeline.rs:1464); UI reads front_index unfenced at 4 sites (frame/present.rs:214, editor_bridge.rs:1568/1708/1756, perform_mode/render.rs:252). TWO MTLDevices (app.rs:2046, 2375 — MTLCreateSystemDefaultDevice x2) => MTLSharedEvent cannot cross => read fence must be CPU-side completion-handler atomics. Tear scenario: GPU saturated, UI sample of front slot s still queued/executing when content frame N+3 overwrites s. Explains main-window + perform-mode tearing under RT load.
2. Output window: CLEAN. Single queue, blit+present in one command buffer (content_pipeline.rs:2687-2727), non-blocking next_drawable skips when starved. Failure mode under saturation = skipped presents (judder), not tearing.
3. Recording: fenced (GpuFence condvar). Export: independent. Pacing: no double-gate, timer slips. TexturePool: frame-stamp recycling, sound because surface wait paces encode <=3 frames ahead of completion.
4. Dead code: output_presenter.rs + metal/vsync.rs — zero references, delete.
FIX DESIGN (per-bridge, CPU atomics on the existing Arc<SharedTextureBridge> — extends existing shared state, none new): read_counter, read_stamp[3], read_retired. UI acquire = loop{ s=front; c=++counter; stamp[s].fetch_max(c); if front==s return (s,c) }; completion handler (or no-sample fallback) retires c. Content reuse adds: front != s AND retired >= stamp[s]. Stalls content under saturation instead of tearing. Liveness: front advances on any newer completion; no deadlock.
VERIFICATION: headless bridge-probe harness (two devices, colour frames, flooded queues, mixed-pixel readback detector) — red before, green after.

title: Traced AO never darkens the environment diffuse term, only the small flat ambient
description: render_scene.wgsl: base_rgb = direct + ibl + ambient + emissive. `ambient` goes through rt_or_flat_ambient(), which with RT on returns albedo * rt_irradiance_mask, and the kernel writes irradiance = ambient_color * ao + gi (raytrace.rs:1451) — so traced AO multiplies ONLY the flat ambient_color (atmosphere.ambient_tint * AMBIENT_IRRADIANCE_SCALE 0.15 * material ambient knob). Meanwhile diffuse_ibl = kd_ibl * albedo * irradiance_map * occlusion uses resolve_occlusion(uv), the material BAKED occlusion texture, untouched by RT. In any HDRI-lit scene the environment diffuse dominates, so turning RT on barely darkens contact regions and corners. Read from the shader, not yet measured; the furnace test on lane/rt-furnace-oracle (test B) is the measurement. Fix shape: route traced AO into the diffuse IBL term too, or combine traced AO with the baked occlusion factor before diffuse_ibl uses it.
close_reason: Fixed by ED-A (landed 3158b4f2): env joins the GI gather at every depth and substitutes the raster irradiance map in fs_pbr, so traced AO now darkens the environment diffuse term. Furnace corner leg (shaded/open ratio) green; RT-off cross-check green. k3 (lead)

comments.text: CONFIRMED by measurement and by looking, on lane/rt-furnace-oracle. Scene: white albedo-1 floor, white albedo-1 plate hovering 0.6 above it, uniform L=1.0 environment via the new node.bake_environment uniform mode, lights 0, material ambient 0.0, rt_enabled true, assert_rt_dispatched passing. Result: open=0.97266 shaded=0.97362 ratio 1.0010 — zero darkening. A frame dump is flat white with no contact shadow anywhere. Three independent confirmations: (1) arithmetic — irradiance = ambient_color * ao + gi, ambient_color = 0 with the ambient knob at 0 and gi = 0 with no sun casters and no emissives, so traced AO multiplies zero; (2) the earlier toggle version measured rt_on == rt_off == 0.49377 byte-identical; (3) the picture. Also caught and fixed a vacuity trap in the gate itself: the occluder was 0.5 grey against a white floor and the probe under it sees the PLATE, so the gate passed at ratio 0.5077 by reading albedo as shade. Occluder is now albedo-1 white; never reintroduce a colour difference. Gate is written and #[ignore]d against this bead. FIX FORK, needs Peter: (a) physical — put the occluded environment diffuse into the RT irradiance term and have render_scene.wgsl SUBSTITUTE rather than add, mirroring the reflection path's existing discipline. No new texture, occlusion denoises for free on the existing accumulate/atrous path, kernel already samples prefiltered_env at RT_REFL_HIT_ENV_DIFFUSE_ROUGHNESS for reflection hits so the primary surface can do the same. Cost: breaks the approved semantic 'ambient knob at 0 = true black with RT on', since an environment-lit surface would stay lit at knob 0. (b) conservative — dedicated full-res AO texture multiplied into diffuse_ibl alongside resolve_occlusion, preserving the knob. Cost: new texture plus its own history ping-pong and atrous channel, because splitting AO out of the irradiance loses the denoising it currently gets for free. Blocked on the semantic call, not on engineering.

title: glTF TANGENT attribute is dropped at import; normal maps use a derived cotangent frame
description: The importer never reads the glTF TANGENT vertex attribute (no Semantic::Tangents read in gltf_load.rs) and MeshVertex has no tangent slot (position 16, normal 16, uv at 32). render_scene.wgsl resolve_normal therefore builds its TBN with cotangent_frame(n, world_pos, uv_t) from screen-space derivatives. Two consequences. (1) Mirrored-handedness UVs get the wrong bitangent sign - NormalTangentMirrorTest.glb ships 80 verts at TANGENT.w = -1 precisely to test this, and its V Mirror / U Mirror columns cannot be correct. (2) A derived frame is unstable at atlas seams, and this asset is a packed atlas, so every tile edge is a derivative discontinuity: measured raster max luma 47.6 with the normal map wired vs 1.31 with the normal_map wire stripped, a 36x blowout localised to tile rims (the blown bright rim outlines Peter reported). Fix shape: read TANGENT at import, add a tangent+handedness field to MeshVertex, thread it through the mesh vertex ABI and the raster shader, use the supplied frame when present and fall back to cotangent_frame only when the asset has no TANGENT. This is a multi-crate vertex-ABI change touching every mesh primitive and shader, not a patch. Also the prerequisite for the RT normal-map bug filed alongside.

comments.text:
TANGENT drop audit complete. See brief below.

## 1. Parse location (TANGENT not read)
File: crates/manifold-renderer/src/node_graph/gltf_load.rs:flatten_primitive (699-765)
- reader.read_tangents() is never called
- Only POSITION, NORMAL, TEXCOORD_0 are consumed
- Drop happens here: attribute simply not read from parsed glTF

## 2. Vertex layout (no tangent field)
File: crates/manifold-renderer/src/generators/mesh_common.rs
- MeshVertex struct (48 bytes): position, normal, uv only
- No tangent field exists

## 3. Normal mapping (derives frame, not vertex attr)
File: crates/manifold-renderer/src/node_graph/primitives/shaders/render_scene.wgsl
- cotangent_frame (760): computes T/B from dpdx/dpdy of position+UV
- resolve_normal (780): always uses derived frame, never reads vertex tangent
- Mikkelsen method, per-fragment derivation

## 4. Other dropped attrs
- NO: JOINTS_0/WEIGHTS_0 are read and used by skin_mesh
- COLOR_0 read but GPU-dropped (report-only)
- Only TANGENT is fully dropped

## 5. Touch seams for adding tangent
1. gltf_load.rs: call reader.read_tangents() 
2. mesh_common.rs: add pub tangent: [f32; 4] field
3. MESH_VERTEX_SPECS: add Vec4F channel descriptor
4. render_scene.wgsl vs-in: add tangent: vec4<f32>
5. render_scene.wgsl resolve_normal: branch on tangent.w != 0
6. Verify CPU consumers (RT accel build, picking) handle stride change

## 6. Test fixtures
- NO existing fixtures with TANGENT found
- Bead mentions synthetic-GLB builders in gltf_import tests.rs
- Red test would reuse those or hand-author minimal glTF JSON

## Fix shape
Phase 1: Read TANGENT in flatten_primitive, populate MeshVertex.tangent (default [0,0,0,1] when absent)
Phase 2: Extend MeshVertex struct + MESH_VERTEX_SPECS
Phase 3: Shader branch on tangent.w != 0, Gram-Schmidt TBN when authored else cotangent_frame fallback
Zero regression: tangent.w=0 default preserves derived-frame path for assets without tangents.

title: RT reflections are normal-map-blind (traced specular uses the vertex normal only)
description: Measured on tests/fixtures/gltf/khronos/NormalTangentMirrorTest.glb with RT + RT Reflections on, env 0.15 / fill 0 / sun 10: the internal refl_raw channel is BIT-IDENTICAL with the normal_map wire bound vs surgically stripped - differing fraction 0.00000, max abs diff 0.0000, both variants lit over the same 0.0897 of the frame. The map never reaches the kernel. Root cause: raytrace.rs fetch_interpolated_normal returns the barycentric-interpolated vertex normal and there is no tangent-space normal-map perturbation anywhere in the RT kernel; RtNormalSource carries no tangent address and no normal-map texture index. Made worse because render_scene.wgsl SUBSTITUTES rt_reflection.rgb for the prefiltered env fetch (never adds), so turning RT Reflections on actively DESTROYS the shape the raster IBL had - a straight regression from raster for every normal-mapped smooth surface. Symptom in app: tiles read as flat/empty with a faint donut and isolated bright specks. Failing gate is written and #[ignore]d against this bead: crates/manifold-renderer/tests/gpu_proofs/rt_normal_tangent_mirror.rs, normal_tangent_mirror_normal_map_reaches_the_traced_reflection. Fix shape: plumb the glTF TANGENT attribute into MeshVertex and RtNormalSource (bindless address + handedness), sample the normal map in-kernel, build the TBN, perturb n before the reflection lobe. Named stopgap alternative: gate the substitution off where a normal map is bound. Blocked on BUG-wfxe (gltf-tangent-attribute-dropped-at-import).
close_reason: Fixed on lane/rt-wytp (merged): the RT kernel now perturbs the primary-hit shading normal with the normal map (analytic per-triangle TBN, mr_tex_index pattern). Gate differing_fraction 0.000 -> 0.122; reflections on normal-mapped surfaces now beat raster instead of regressing it. k3 (lead)

title: glTF-imported material params silently dropped in instantiate_def (blocks BUG-pt6g end-to-end)
description: Symptom: glTF-imported materials (via assemble_import_graph -> flatten_groups -> PresetRuntime::from_def_with_device) do not respond to param overrides applied post-import to the flattened def -- confirmed on node.pbr_material ambient and node.bake_environment intensity on tests/fixtures/gltf/the_rosetta_stone.glb: mutating def.nodes params after flatten_groups() correctly changes the def (verified via print), but the rendered output is byte-identical across a 0.05->0.9 ambient sweep and a 0.2->3.0 env intensity sweep. Root cause: unknown, suspects narrowed via source instrumentation earlier this session -- graph_loader.rs instantiate_def (or one of its 4 migration passes: migrate_def_type_ids, migrate_scene_object_wires, migrate_gltf_anim_v2, flatten_groups) silently drops SOME node params (confirmed: bake_equirect_envmap intensity reads its primitive-declared default 1.0 regardless of the def override) while others survive fine (mode param on the same node persists correctly) -- the override loop in graph_loader.rs:679-704 looks structurally correct/unconditional on read, so the drop happens somewhere between a correct-looking write and the primitive run() read. Fix shape: instrument/bisect instantiate_def one migration stage at a time (print node.params before/after each) to find which stage clobbers which params. This blocks real-world verification of BUG-pt6g (lighting macros dead on photoscan imports) -- the unlit-routing fix (this session, lane/unlit-default-lit) is structurally correct and unit-tested, but end-to-end on a real GLB is still dark because of this separate bug. Likely the same mechanism as "the binding-replant bug" the team lead flagged as split into its own bead -- confirm and dedupe before starting new work on it.

title: Binding default_value replant clobbers live node.params on every graph rebuild (BUG-303 relapse class)
description: Mechanism (lane-confirmed with instrumentation, 2026-07-30): card-stamped defs (GLB imports via stamp_scene_node_exposures_into, scene_exposure.rs:166-255) give EVERY node param a BindingDef whose default_value is a frozen snapshot of node.params at stamp time. On every graph build, instantiate_def (graph_loader.rs:679-704) correctly writes def node.params onto the live node, then BoundGraph::new -> apply_binding_defaults (param_binding.rs:629-648) unconditionally replants every binding default_value over it. Two copies of one fact, nothing keeps them in sync — any writer touching node.params for a bound target (def edits, migrations, direct macro/mapping writes) is silently reverted at next rebuild. This is the BUG-303 (import values clobbered to primitive defaults) class relapsed; the old fix only synced the copies at stamp time. Fix direction chosen by lead: ROOT (option B) — remove the duplicate source of truth: seed the binding skip-cache from the live graph value instead of replanting default_value. CAUTION: bound_graph.rs binding lifecycle is load-bearing (OilyFluid Speed regression 903deaa8; apply_inner_overrides cache-clear contract) — own slice with full-context review, not a quick lane. Also: dropped/reverted param writes must become loud. Regression test shape: import fixture, mutate a bound param post-stamp, assert it survives a rebuild.
notes: Bisect result (2026-07-30, CPU-only repro: post-assembly def mutation of bake_environment intensity, survives-rebuild check): BROKEN at every testable commit back to 6b02cba0 (2026-07-12, the commit that ADDED the intensity param + card binding) — no introducing commit; defect born with the param. Mechanism older still: bound_graph.rs traces to 652486d9 (shared BoundGraph unification). BUG-303 (import transforms clobbered, fixed 66772e69/995006eb 2026-07-22) diagnosed the same mechanism against a different symptom — confirmed recurring class. Note: the ParamManifest per-frame path (bound.apply) is IMMUNE — live macro sliders are unaffected by this bug; it bites def edits, migrations, and any direct node.params writer.

Suspects, sharpest first: (1) the RT ambient floor — render_scene.rs:4097 passes ambient_tint * AMBIENT_IRRADIANCE_SCALE * scene_ambient, where scene_ambient is the max MATERIAL ambient knob (scene_params[1]), not env intensity — env=0 does not zero it; (2) the shadow vis term (out_sv) may be gating ambient/GI in the composite, not just the direct sun term — then vis changes from sun movement alter total light even at intensity 0; (3) GI/refl traced terms (raytrace.rs:1153) add hit_emissive + albedo*diffuse_env regardless of sun. Fix shape: dump out_sv/out_irr at sun=0/env=0 in rt-capture (same probe method as BUG-jddy arms), find which term is nonzero, then make intensity-0 mean true black on the RT path exactly as the raster path already does.
close_reason: Root cause: RT secondary rays (AO/GI/reflection) shared the shadow ray's sun-biased origin — sun below a surface sank origins inside geometry, crushing AO/emissive GI, so sun position changed lighting at intensity 0. Fixed on main c79ccd2b (normal-biased sec_origin). Live-verified by Peter in brokenLamp.manifold.

title: RT GI+reflections die when scene goes static (root cause open; stopgap on lane/rt-static-death)
description: RT (GI+reflections) dies ~5 frames after the last object-transform change and never recovers while the scene is static; shadow/AO unaffected. Reproduced headlessly (rt-capture --disable-driver-at/--paused on RtLightTesting.manifold): trace dispatches every frame (probe-verified), rt_ready/accel.ready/casters all healthy, yet GI goes exactly 0 and refl rays all-miss, deterministically; composite bleeds to RT-off baseline over ~90 frames. Never observed alive on a frame without an accel refit. Root cause UNKNOWN — suspect: something the refit refreshes (CPU instance-buffer write / GPU refit command / ready-flag flip) is load-bearing for the GI+reflection resource path (gi_materials buffer, material texture table, or encoder bind state). STOPGAP on branch lane/rt-static-death (commit 1280a1be, worktree slot-1): forced refit every frame — proven in harness + in-app 2026-07-26, NOT LANDED. Root-fix shape: decompose the refit into its 3 actions (CPU write / GPU command / flag flip), test each alone in the harness; the one that keeps RT alive is the mechanism. Startup anomaly to check at landing: RT took ~f30-f120 to first appear in stopgap runs (was <f30 before).
close_reason: FIXED ef59f615 (2026-07-27): root cause = Metal driver reclaims resources no submitted command declares usage on. Static scene -> no refits -> TLAS-referenced BLASes + instance buffer undeclared for frames; GI/refl ray paths (the ones following instance data) read reclaimed memory ~5 frames later; shadow/AO survived because traversal is self-contained in the TLAS. Fix: useResource(Read) on TLAS, every BLAS, and the instance buffer in dispatch_compute_with_accel. Proven by 5-arm forced-refit bisect: write/commit/handler exonerated, refit op cured, useResource cured without refit. The 2026-07-26 constant->device change was NOT the root fix (stays as hygiene). 41/41 RT gpu-proofs.

comments.author: glm-4.7 (dispatcher)
comments.text:
Dispatcher read-only mechanism findings (no probes, no code changes). Companion to /tmp/manifold_seam_review.md (K3's dispatch-gate review). Fable to review.

== The discriminator ==

Shadow/AO/GI/reflection are ONE kernel, ONE dispatch, ONE accel binding (render_scene.rs:4240 calls dispatch_shadow_rays once per RT-ready frame; kernel at raytrace.rs ~L840 casts all four ray types from the same origin, same accel, same walk_with_alpha_test). Therefore any dispatch-level failure theory (encoder cache, command-queue ordering, accel coherence) predicts shadow rays die too. They survive. The failure is DOWNSTREAM of accel traversal, INSIDE the kernel — something GI+reflection read that shadow does not.

That thing is `n` — the interpolated vertex normal at the primary-ray hit (raytrace.rs:885):
- GI: cosine_hemisphere(n, ...) (L1007). Bad n -> rays miss upward -> emissive-hit term -> 0. Matches symptom.
- Reflection: reflect(-V, n) (L1078). Bad n -> rays all-miss. Matches symptom.
- Shadow: biases along p.sun_dir, NEVER n (comment L921 "bias along sun_dir ONLY, not n"). Unaffected. Matches symptom.
- AO: also uses n (L969). Bug says AO survives — OPEN THREAD (Peter suggests this may be observation-level: AO is the subtle channel, a uniform darkening reads as "still working" if not specifically probed).

`n` is read via the bindless normal_sources buffer (RtNormalSource.vertex_base_addr = vertex_buffer.gpu_address() + vertex_offset, raytrace.rs:1981).

== Mechanism candidates, ranked ==

M1 (FAVORED) — normal_sources stale/invalid read under no-refit. ensure_normal_sources (raytrace.rs:1925) rewrites the CPU-mapped rt_normal_sources buffer every RT-ready frame (render_scene.rs:3976). No useResource: for this buffer (the comment at types.rs:238 argues the bound accel transitively makes BLAS vertex buffers resident — true for vertex/index data referenced by the accel geometry, but normal_sources is a SEPARATE kernel-read buffer, not referenced by the accel structure itself). The STOPGAP's refit opens its own device.raw_queue().commandBuffer() (raytrace.rs:406) — a fresh command buffer that may act as an implicit ordering/coherence point on the queue. Static scene, no refit, no ordering point, CPU-mapped writes become unreliable to the trace dispatch.

M2 — general per-dispatch useResource: absence. dispatch_compute_with_accel (encoder.rs:521) never calls useResource: or useHeap: anywhere in manifold-gpu (verified: only two hits, both comments). The "no separate useResource needed" comment at raytrace.rs:1844 is correct ONLY for resources referenced by the accel geometry, not for gi_materials/normal_sources/params_buffer/obj_motion/material textures. M1 may be a specific instance of M2.

M3 — material_textures table staleness via encoder-bind-cache-invalidation bug class. Plausible per-channel split but symptom is "refls all-miss" (walk_with_alpha_test returns false), not "wrong-colored" — texture staleness produces wrong colors not traversal miss. Less favored.

REJECTED — dispatch-level / queue-ordering theories. Cannot explain why shadow+AO survive in a shared dispatch.

== Why the STOPGAP works under M1/M2 ==

Not because the refit fixes the accel (accel was fine — shadow rays prove it) but because the refit's fresh command buffer is an implicit ordering/coherence point on the queue. Static scene, no refit, no ordering point, CPU-mapped writes unreliable. The STOPGAP's correctness depends on a side effect, not the documented refit contract — why it's a stopgap not a fix.

== Fix shape (lead to steer) ==

1. Declare kernel-read buffers on the trace dispatch via useResource: in dispatch_compute_with_accel (encoder.rs:521) — root fix, removes the dependence on the refit's side-effect ordering. Usage: .read for inputs, .write for the four output textures.
2. CHEAPER EXPERIMENT FIRST: the encoder already has compute_memory_barrier_buffers() (encoder.rs:635). Try one line — encoder.compute_memory_barrier_buffers() before tracer.dispatch_shadow_rays at render_scene.rs:4240, remove the stopgap, run the static-scene harness. If RT stays alive, the root cause was coherence not resource declaration — smaller fix. If only useResource fixes it, it was declaration. Both valid, different layers.
3. Delete STOPGAP (render_scene.rs:4058-4073 + rt_frames_since_refit field).
4. Stale-comment cleanup: "no separate useResource needed" comments at raytrace.rs:1844 and types.rs:238 must be removed/rewritten — they are now wrong.

== Cheapest confirmation experiment ==

3-action decomposition already in BUG-jddy: if M1/M2 is right, the "GPU refit command" action ALONE (enqueue an empty/no-op command buffer on device.raw_queue() between CPU writes and trace dispatch, no instance-buffer rewrite, no flag flip) should keep RT alive. If it does -> M1/M2 confirmed.

== File:line anchors ==

- render_scene.rs:3976 — ensure_normal_sources call (CPU writes normal_sources incl vertex_base_addr, no barrier)
- render_scene.rs:4190 — CPU writes gi_materials via mapped pointer, no barrier
- render_scene.rs:4058-4073 — STOPGAP forced-refit block
- render_scene.rs:4240 — single dispatch_shadow_rays call (shared dispatch)
- raytrace.rs:375-425 — refit_accel opens its own commandBuffer() (suspected implicit ordering point)
- raytrace.rs:885 — n = fetch_interpolated_normal(normal_sources, ...) [GI/refl depend, shadow does not]
- raytrace.rs:921-931 — shadow bias along sun_dir NOT n [the asymmetry]
- raytrace.rs:1007 — GI uses cosine_hemisphere(n, ...)
- raytrace.rs:1078 — Reflection uses reflect(-V, n)
- raytrace.rs:1844 / types.rs:238 — the now-wrong "no separate useResource needed" comments
- encoder.rs:521-626 — dispatch_compute_with_accel never calls useResource:/useHeap:
- encoder.rs:625 — compute_cache.clear() after accel dispatch [encoder-bind-cache-invalidation neighborhood]
- encoder.rs:635 — existing compute_memory_barrier_buffers() [the cheaper-fix primitive]

== Open threads for Fable ==

1. AO-discrepancy — bug says AO survives but AO uses n. Likely observation-level (Peter: "not knowing what I am looking at — potentially"). One targeted probe settles it.
2. M1 (normal_sources-specific) vs M2 (general missing-useResource) — predict same symptom, M2 is the more general hazard M1 sits inside.
3. useResource vs memoryBarrierWithScope — different layers, both valid; cheaper experiment (barrier first) bisects.

title: BUG-326 — rt-depth-snapshot-wrong-on-imported-glb-scenes
description:
### BUG-326 (rt-depth-snapshot-wrong-on-imported-glb-scenes) — RT primary rays miss on imported glb scenes: the depth snapshot holds near-zero values at object pixels, wp reconstruction is garbage, reflections black, AO/shadow degraded
**Status:** OPEN
**Severity:** HIGH — RT reflections unusable on imported hero assets (AMG GT3 renders black with `rt_reflections` on); RT AO/shadows subtly wrong on the same scenes (Peter 2026-07-25: "shadows look odd at times where I would expect AO"). Hand-authored probe scenes pass, which masked this.
**Symptom:** AMG GT3 (`tests/fixtures/gltf/mercedes-amg_gt3__www.vecarz.com.glb`) with RT on + `rt_reflections` on renders black/textureless (non-black fraction 0.024 vs 0.096 baseline). Originally read as Base traced reflections (R1)'s v1 shading gap; the Raster-parity reflections build landed (`7ad9bd36`) and the render stayed BYTE-IDENTICAL, proving the shading change never reached the image.
**Root cause (proven 2026-07-25, K3 kernel-probe chain):** the reflection block is gated on `obj_id >= 0` from the PRIMARY visibility ray (`crates/manifold-gpu/src/metal/raytrace.rs` `trace_shadow_rays`). On imported glb scenes that ray misses at (almost) every shaded pixel: `opaque_depth_snapshot` holds near-zero values at object pixels (AMG ≈ 0.0003–0.005, DamagedHelmet ≈ 0.009–0.04 — measured via temporary kernel debug writing `depth_tex.read(gpix,0)` into `out_refl`), while the hand-authored R1 grid scene holds proper standard-z ≈ 0.995 at its probe pixel (verified numerically: on=1.1 = depth 0.995 × LUT weight ≈ 1.1). `world_pos_from_depth` (standard-z inverse, far = `>= 1.0-1e-6`) reconstructs near-plane garbage, the `dist*1e-3`-bounded primary ray stops centimetres out and misses, the block's else writes zeros, and the WGSL substitution (`rt_flags.x`) replaces the specular env with those zeros → black. Every shading-path debug variant (albedo-only, env-only, constant env sample) left the render byte-identical, confining the fault to the depth/wp/primary-ray path, NOT the reflection shading (Raster-parity's env-at-hit term is proven live by `rt_r1_reflection::raster_parity_env_at_hit_adds_env_term` on the hand-authored fixture).
**Unknown (next oracle):** WHY imported scenes write tiny depth while hand-authored scenes write standard-z. Suspects, ranked: (a) the import graph's `camera_lens` node (probes lack it) alters the projection the E2a prepass uses vs what `world_pos_from_depth` assumes; (b) the E2a prepass (`render_scene.rs:3762`, `shadow_pipeline` + camera `view_proj`) emits a different z convention for these scenes; (c) synthesized import camera near/far defaults. Cheapest discriminator: add a `camera_lens` node to the R1 grid scene and re-measure probe-pixel depth — a flip to tiny values convicts the lens.
**Fix shape:** depends on (a)/(b)/(c): honour the actual z convention in `world_pos_from_depth` (if scene-variant-but-legitimate), or make the prepass write standard-z (if the convention is a bug). Plus a gpu-proof that renders an IMPORTED glb through the RT path asserting primary-hit coverage above a threshold, so this class can't hide behind hand-authored fixtures again.
**Exonerated (2026-07-25, Flash-lane experiment matrix on the R1 grid fixture, debug-kernel depth readout):** `camera_lens` (depth identical with/without: on=1.1002 both) and import camera params (tilt 0.3/fov 0.9: on=0.7965 = different geometry at the probe pixel, not corrupted depth). Remaining suspects: an untested split between the gpu-test harness path (works) and the render-import/in-app runtime path (broken) — same scene through both paths is the next discriminator — or import-graph content beyond the camera (env nodes, transmission, object count).
**Lead seam review (2026-07-25, k3 — full text `/tmp/manifold_seam_review.md`):** the ENTIRE static write/read path is exonerated element-by-element: one `view_proj` local feeds prepass (3769), raster (3264), and `inv_view_proj` (3979); prepass consumes the SAME `ObjectDraw.uniforms.model` as the raster (3635 shares by reference); `shadow_depth.wgsl` writes plain `clip.z/clip.w` (no remap); the batch CLEARS to 1.0 (encoder.rs:1326 — stale-texture theory dead); snapshot is single-sample Depth32Float with correct usage; RT dispatch binds it at texture(0) with no slot collision; gltf meshes are 48-byte `MeshVertex` soup so `vcount`/stride match. **Geometric contradiction:** tiny standard-z ⟺ object pixels at z ∈ [1.0003·n, 1.04·n] — a mm-thin shell at the near plane, geometrically incompatible with a correctly-framed raster image of a 4.5 m car under ANY single-view perspective; the import auto-frame near (`min(0.05, front_margin·0.5)`, scene.rs:171) analytically yields d ∈ [0.5, 0.98]. So either (A) the GPU prepass draw diverges from the CPU matrix math at draw time (bindings/pipeline/vertex-pull level), (B) runtime `view_proj`/`model` VALUES are degenerate (invisible statically), or (C) texture identity at dispatch ≠ texture written (no static evidence). **Next oracle (lane-delegated one-shot probe):** CPU-project known points with the runtime matrices AND read back the GPU snapshot at the same pixels in ONE render_import run on DamagedHelmet — CPU≈0.98/GPU≈0.003 convicts the draw level (A); CPU≈GPU≈0.003 moves the bug to import scene assembly (B).
**Edge note:** probes can pass for the wrong reason — a far-garbage wp still lets the primary ray cross real geometry because `max_distance` scales with wp distance. Probe fixtures should assert wp sanity (probe-pixel depth in a stated standard-z band), not only final image values.
**Probe round 2 (2026-07-25 PM, Flash lane `bug326-depth-probe`, env-gated `MANIFOLD_BUG326_PROBE` raw readback, commit `a2373535`):** the tiny-depth measurement DOES NOT REPRODUCE with a trustworthy oracle. Raw `copy_texture_to_buffer` readback of `opaque_depth_snapshot` (no PNG/LUT in the path): DamagedHelmet GPU 0.983 vs CPU-expected 0.986; AMG GT3 GPU 0.765 vs CPU 0.741; temporal_upscale on/off identical; global min/max/mean healthy (AMG 0.606/1.0/0.936). Git history shows NO renderer code landed between the morning's tiny-depth measurement and this probe — so the morning's numbers were almost certainly an ARTIFACT of its readout path (depth written into `out_refl`, read back through the tonemapped PNG LUT — scene-exposure-dependent, and the import scenes carry IBL/env the grid scene lacks). The depth-corruption theory of the black render is thereby DEMOTED; the live question is whether the black-render symptom itself (non-black 0.024 vs 0.096, byte-identical across shading variants) still reproduces — round 3 measures that matrix. If it does, the next instrument is a RAW primary-hit/obj_id coverage counter in `trace_shadow_rays` (never a PNG readout).
notes: EVIDENCE CHALLENGED 2026-07-25 (Opus code review, opposite-space pass). The "near-zero depth on imported scenes" number is a MEASUREMENT ARTIFACT, not a depth reading. out_refl is only observable through the shaded image (gpu_proofs/rt_r1_reflection.rs reads final-target luminance), and fs_pbr consumes the substituted value as `specular_ibl = prefiltered * (F0*env_brdf.x + env_brdf.y)` (render_scene.wgsl:1541). Every debug value written into out_refl is therefore scaled by that per-pixel split-sum weight. The R1 grid probes weight ~1.1 (ground material metallic 1.0 / roughness 0.01 / albedo 0.8 — the "LUT weight ~1.1" already noted in the R1 handoff); imported dielectric/dark-metal materials weight 0.001-0.05. 0.995 x 1.1 = 1.1 (grid), 0.99 x 0.04 = 0.04 (DamagedHelmet), 0.995 x 0.003 = 0.003 (AMG). The whole 300-3000x "wrong depth" spread is the material weight. Suspects (a) camera_lens, (b) prepass z convention, (c) near/far defaults are aimed at an artifact — do not spend the morning there without first reading the depth snapshot DIRECTLY (readback of opaque_depth_snapshot, or a full-frame constant write into out_refl) rather than through fs_pbr. ALSO: the "raster-parity build left the render BYTE-IDENTICAL" evidence is weak, not proof the change never reached the image. Asset facts (read from tests/fixtures/gltf/mercedes-amg_gt3__www.vecarz.com.glb, 78 materials, NO metallicRoughness textures — all factors): the largest group is roughness 0.958, and ~half the materials sit above the refl cutoff+band (0.6+0.1), so those pixels take the no-ray above-cutoff branch (raytrace.rs:1067-1070) and never cast a reflection ray at all; the raster-parity change only touched the reflection-ray HIT branch, and on a hero car over a void background most rays that DO cast escape to the env miss branch. Byte-identity is expected either way. THIRD: metallicFactor is 1.0 on ~90% of the AMG materials, so the car is a full metal in fs_pbr — no diffuse term, its entire appearance IS the specular-env fetch RT substitutes. That is why a zero from RT paints this asset literally black while a dielectric test scene would only look dull; it is an amplifier of the fault, not the fault.
